results.reason: The memo never raises the Delivery Date conflict between Schedule §1.1 (ship date) and MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester). It also does not discuss Harlow losing remedies for transit delays.
There is no recommendation to conform the Schedule's Delivery Date definition to the MSA, and no order-of-precedence fix.

Issue 2 identifies the §4.3 scope of all housings and similar components worldwide, against the Term Sheet's Series 7 / U.S. bargain. It explains the blocking of non-U.S. plants and other suppliers, and recommends narrowing to Series 7 in the U.S.

Issue 3 identifies the one-sided §15.2 assignment right, including to a competitor. It explains the risks to supply continuity and the Specifications, and recommends requiring consent, barring competitors and adding a change-of-control termination right.

Issue 1 explains that Amendment §2.1 and §2.2 remove gross negligence and the IP indemnity from the cap exclusions, so those losses fall under the 12-month fee cap. It recommends rejecting the change and restoring the original exclusions.
The memo states the §11.1 cap is fees paid in the prior 12 months and lists the original §11.2 exclusions: gross negligence, willful misconduct and the IP Indemnity.
The memo states Term Sheet §3.1 limits exclusivity to Series 7 Housings within the U.S. and uses it as the baseline for comparing MSA §4.3.
The memo states New York law governs under MSA §16.1. It flags that NY law points need confirmation and cites no cases or statutes.
The memo is structured for the partner. Each issue gives location, why it matters and a recommended fix. Issues are ranked by importance, and there is an assumptions and open points section.
The memo explicitly treats the Term Sheet only as evidence of the deal. It notes the 3-year term and 45-day payment terms are not defects.
Issues are attributed to the correct documents and sections, with no party reversal. No legal authority is cited, and the NY public-policy point is flagged as needing confirmation.
